name: Vendor report in one tap
summary: Vendor report in one tap: reads each listing's record and open homes from VaultRE, drafts the report to the vendor in Outlook once the agent has written the commentary, and queues the send for one approval. Crons read and draft; a person approves every send.

listing-report.evidence: no discovery call describes this yet (1 call read, 0 describe a vendor report); steps come from the workflow spec

covered_by.stats-export: cron pull (VaultRE listing record and open homes; portal views and enquiries are a gap)
covered_by.weekly-figures: cron pull (open homes in the window)
covered_by.check-figures: skill (the agent checks the figures before commentary is written)
covered_by.write-commentary: skill (the agent writes commentary into the store)
covered_by.manager-review: approval (principal reviews the Outlook draft before the one-tap send)
covered_by.send-report: approval (one tap sends the Outlook draft)
covered_by.record-keeping: draft (VaultRE activity note on the property)

crons.name: pull
crons.summary: Read each listing's record and open homes from VaultRE (7am Monday to Friday in Sydney).

crons.name: draft
crons.summary: Draft each listing's vendor report in Outlook and queue its send for approval, once commentary is written.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: a read of a property or its open homes, an Outlook draft that a person still has to send, and an activity note on the property record. Sending the Outlook draft is a live operation and waits for a person.

vaultre.covers: listing record and open homes read; activity note as the internal record

microsoft-365.covers: Outlook draft to the vendor and the one-tap send

rex.covers: listing record read (heading, address, price); no open homes, no note written

gaps: Rex: a business sets platform to rex in settings, and each vendor's property_id is the Rex listing id. The report's heading, address and price come from listings.read. Open homes are not read, because the Rex docs read do not show how a calendar event is marked as an open home or linked to a listing in a search; the report then leaves the open home section out and says nothing about open homes. No note is written to the listing (no listing note in the pages read), and Rex's vendor feedback is not used. Not confirmed on a live account: the listing fields on the read (listing_adverts, price_advertise_as, property.system_search_key) with default fields.

Portal figures (views, enquiries, inspections) are not mapped: realestate.com.au's Campaign API and Console Cloud have no operations in the kit. Their platform maps are needed before the report carries portal numbers.
The VaultRE owner list and feedback summary have no typed response schema in the vendor spec, so the vendor's email is set in settings instead of read from the owner record.
PropertyMe, the tool named on the outside call, has no platform in the kit.
No command or shell form yet writes commentary into the store under commentary. tools/workflow.ts only has propose, which is quoting's. Until one exists, the draft cron waits at needs-commentary.
Commentary, the manager review, vendor questions and price review calls are judgment steps. Vendor questions and price review calls are not covered by any cron or skill.
Both adapters are docs-only: VaultRE is status spec with offline tests only, and the Microsoft 365 token flow is not built (a Graph access token is supplied by hand).

evidence.calls: 1 call read for this workflow; 0 describe how they make a vendor report, so the steps come from the spec
evidence.platforms: vendor help centres for console-cloud, realestate-com-au and rex read. Rex is mapped in the kit (listing read used here); console-cloud and realestate-com-au have no mapped operations. The workflow runs on VaultRE or Rex for the listing, and Microsoft 365 for the email.
